newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka president brother claims damages.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka president brother claims damages.

text.p: The estranged brother of Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has been allowed by the Supreme Court to bring a human rights case against the government, officials said on Wednesday.

Anura Bandaranaike, a lawmaker of the main opposition United National Party, is seeking 25 million rupees ($433,275) as compensation from the government for an alleged arbitary search of his house by police last month.
Bandaranaike's house was searched on suspicion he was hiding a suspect, a UNP lawmaker, wanted by police for the killing of a ruling People's Alliance parliament deputy Nalanda Ellawala.

"The search was done with mischief and with political motivation," Bandaranaike told Reuters. "The (suspect UNP lawmaker) could never have come into my house because this is a high security area and in the same compound where my mother (Prime Minister Sirimavo Bandaranaike) also lives."
Bandaranaike said he was confident of winning the case, now that the Supreme Court has allowed him to bring it.
Criminal investigation department sleuths had entered his house forcibly late on the night of February 12 without a search warrant, Bandaranaike said.
His lawyers said since police had searched his house without a warrant Bandaranaike had been subjected to unequal treatment before the law.
Court officials said the case will come up for hearing on July 11. Top police officials have been named as respondents in the case.
Ellawala was killed during a roadside brawl between his and UNP supporters in the southern Ratnapura district. A UNP lawmaker and a former UNP mayor are now in police custody over the killing.

Anura Bandaranaike was in his mother's Sri Lanka Freedom Party, the main constituent of the ruling People's Alliance, until he fell out with his sister over party leadership and joined the opposition before the 1994 general election.
But he still has good relations with his mother and the two live in the same compund in Colombo's high-security Rosmead Place locality.
